steps.instruction: Read the request and declared evidence. Bind the frozen backend commit, repository-owned suite command, attested endpoint and served head, authorization, account by credential name, seed namespace and new run identity. Confirm the served head contains the pinned commit. Do not derive another endpoint or author a case.

reads.when: when the backend checkout is bound

calls.purpose: Read only the request and declared evidence.
Verify pinned-to-served ancestry without changing Git state.

produces: A frozen API run binding and prerequisite classification.

steps.instruction: Probe the exact attested endpoint before running cases. Resolve credentials only at the suite boundary and never persist values. Stop if the endpoint, authority, account, seed or suite is unavailable.

calls.purpose: Probe the exact attested API endpoint.

steps.instruction: Run the repository-owned command as an external client against the bound endpoint and namespace. Retain the complete runner output and exit status. Do not alter the suite or product source.

calls.purpose: Run the exact declared API suite command.

steps.instruction: Copy every runner-reported case, read created records back through the API, judge contract, data and lifecycle lanes separately, then delete exactly the run namespace. Produce concrete defects and targeted repair instructions for failed criteria; never invent missing case evidence.

calls.purpose: Read back and remove only records in the bound run namespace.
calls.when: when the suite created namespace data

produces: Concrete failed-criterion feedback or passing review results.

steps.instruction: Write an append-only verification record and response with actual artifact hashes, observations and review results. Never overwrite an earlier run. Validate the records and present only a fully passing result as done.

calls.purpose: Write immutable verification and response records.
Run scripts/validate_operator.py against the request and response.
Present case and lane results with raw evidence references.
